cards.explanation: The answer is Babylon is captured. The LORD says to lift up a banner and “hold nothing back…” (Jeremiah 50:2). You don't raise a banner for small news, friends. That's the kind of announcement you make with both hands in the air and a mustache to match.

The answer is False. The idols don't come through in one piece. The announcement says Bel is put to shame and Marduk is shattered, and her images are disgraced and her idols are broken in pieces (Jeremiah 50:2). Bel and Marduk are Babylon's false gods. I've dropped a tray of cookies, and even that's a gentler landing.

The answer is a desolation. A nation from the north will come against Babylon and make her land a desolation (Jeremiah 50:3). No one will live in it, and both man and beast will flee. Nobody is left to even turn off the lights.

The answer is the children of Israel and Judah. The LORD says the children of Israel and the children of Judah will come together, weeping as they come, and will seek the LORD their God (Jeremiah 50:4). Two groups, one direction. Tissues for everybody.

The answer is False. This covenant doesn't run out. They will join themselves to the LORD in “…an everlasting covenant that will never be forgotten.” (Jeremiah 50:5). I've lost track of plenty of things in my time, including a whole drawer's worth of years. This covenant will never be forgotten.
The answer is resting. The LORD says His people have wandered from mountain to hill and “…have forgotten their resting place.” (Jeremiah 50:6). Somebody get these folks a chair.

The answer is that Israel's enemies say they're not guilty since Israel sinned against the LORD. Those enemies said, “We are not guilty, for they have sinned against the LORD, their true pasture, the LORD, the hope of their fathers.” (Jeremiah 50:7). It's a tidy excuse, and it names the LORD twice.

The answer is to flee from the midst of Babylon. The LORD says, “Flee from the midst of Babylon; depart from the land of the Chaldeans…” (Jeremiah 50:8). When the LORD says go, nobody needs to stay behind to fold the napkins.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “For behold, I stir up and bring against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the land of the north.” (Jeremiah 50:9). That's the reason the call to leave comes first, friends. Staying put in a place with that coming is a hard plan to defend.
The answer is False. The plunderers leave full. The LORD says, “Chaldea will be plundered; all who plunder her will have their fill…” (Jeremiah 50:10). Nobody walks away with an empty box here.

The answer is least. The LORD says the plunderers' mother will be greatly ashamed, and “Behold, she will be the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.” (Jeremiah 50:12). That's a long fall from the loud celebration just before it. They were frolicking like a heifer treading grain, and now it's a dry land.

The answer is False. Nobody stops to admire her. Because of the wrath of the LORD, she will not be inhabited and will become completely desolate. “All who pass through Babylon will be horrified and will hiss at all her wounds.” (Jeremiah 50:13). Horrified and hissing is the opposite of admiring.

The answer is that she has sinned against the LORD. He doesn't leave the archers guessing, friends. He says, “Shoot at her! Spare no arrows! For she has sinned against the LORD.” (Jeremiah 50:14). Orders and reason come in the same breath. That's like a recipe that tells you the oven temperature and why, and I'd bake a lot more batches if all my recipes did that.

The answer is that she has thrown up her hands in surrender. The LORD calls for a war cry against her on every side, and the text says, “She has thrown up her hands in surrender; her towers have fallen; her walls are torn down.” (Jeremiah 50:15). Surrender, fallen towers and torn-down walls all sit in the same verse.

The answer is same. The LORD says, “Since this is the vengeance of the LORD, take out your vengeance upon her; as she has done, do the same to her.” (Jeremiah 50:15). The measure is what she has done, friends. Same deed, same treatment.

The answer is True. That's what the text says. The LORD says, “In the face of the oppressor’s sword, each will turn to his own people, each will flee to his own land.” (Jeremiah 50:16). Everybody heads for home. I know that feeling of wanting to head home, believe me.

The answer is the king of Assyria. The LORD says, “The first to devour him was the king of Assyria; the last to crush his bones was Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.” (Jeremiah 50:17). Nebuchadnezzar is the king of Babylon, and he's named last.

The answer is True. The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says, “I will punish the king of Babylon and his land as I punished the king of Assyria.” (Jeremiah 50:18). The LORD names the Assyrian king in the same breath. Babylon's king isn't getting a different rulebook.

The answer is satisfied. The LORD says, “I will return Israel to his pasture, and he will graze on Carmel and Bashan; his soul will be satisfied on the hills of Ephraim and Gilead.” (Jeremiah 50:19). Grazing on Carmel and Bashan comes right before it. Think of the feeling when you finally sit down after a long shift on your feet, only bigger.

The answer is none, friends. The LORD says, “…a search will be made for Israel’s guilt, but there will be none…” (Jeremiah 50:20). Somebody goes looking and comes back empty-handed, which is the best kind of empty. The same verse says, “for I will forgive the remnant I preserve.” (Jeremiah 50:20).
